quality_snapshot.text:
Lena huddled beneath the cracked awning of the café, the rain drumming heavily against the pavement, each drop pooling in the gutters where neon lights flickered like lost souls in a storm. With her breath visible in the chill, she wrapped her arms tightly around herself, fingers grazing the worn leather of her jacket, its familiar texture now feeling strangely foreign, as if the warmth of her memories were fading into the mist surrounding her.

“Hey, you okay?” Marco’s voice sliced through the relentless patter of rain. His silhouette emerged from the downpour, framed by the flickering sign above the café, the words “Café Sol” barely visible. He stepped closer, boots splashing through shallow puddles, sending droplets scattering like tiny shards of glass.

“Yeah, just… thinking,” she replied, her voice almost drowned by the rain. Shifting her weight from one foot to the other, she felt the cold seep through the thin soles of her shoes. The inviting warmth of the café beckoned her, the rich aroma of roasted coffee beans and sweet pastries wafting through the air, yet it felt as intangible as a distant memory, just out of reach.

“Thinking? Or avoiding?” Marco leaned against the brick wall, crossing his arms. A hint of a smile danced at the corners of his mouth, the kind that always seemed to peel back her defenses, smooth as a knife slicing through butter.

“Both, maybe,” she admitted, her gaze dropping to the swirling puddles at their feet. The chaos above mirrored the turmoil within her, the reflected colors and shadows swirling like a tempest. “I just… don’t know if I want to go in there.”

“Why not?” he pressed, his brow furrowing slightly, concern etching lines across his forehead. “It’s just coffee. We can sit, talk, and you can tell me what’s really going on.”
